name: Differential Diffusion Theory for Participating Media
definition: A physically-based differentiable rendering framework for participating media that uses diffusion approximation to compute gradients of radiance with respect to scene parameters (density, absorption, lighting) efficiently, avoiding the high cost of backpropagation or finite differences.
summary: Differential Diffusion Theory is a differentiable rendering framework that computes scene parameter derivatives by solving the diffusion equation, replacing expensive Monte Carlo path tracing with fast PDE solvers for real-time optimization.
